future.mizu: Parallel Future Backend using ‘mizu’

Note: This package is an early prototype under development.

Introduction

The future.mizu package is a backend for the future framework, also known as the Futureverse. The Futureverse makes it easy to parallelize existing R code - often with only a minor change of code. Most users interact with it via higher-level packages such as futurize, future.apply, furrr, and doFuture, and you choose where and how the code runs by setting a future backend with plan(). This package adds the mizu_multisession backend, which runs futures in parallel on the local machine using the mizu package.

library(futurize)
plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession)  # parallelize on the current machine

# A slow function
slow_fcn <- function(x) {
  Sys.sleep(1.0)
  x^2
}

# Example data
xs <- 1:10

# Sequential and parallel base R apply
ys <- lapply(xs, slow_fcn)
ys <- lapply(xs, slow_fcn) |> futurize()

# Sequential and parallel purrr map
library(purrr)
ys <- xs |> map(slow_fcn)
ys <- xs |> map(slow_fcn) |> futurize()

# Sequential and parallel foreach calls
library(foreach)
ys <- foreach(x = xs) %do% slow_fcn(x)
ys <- foreach(x = xs) %do% slow_fcn(x) |> futurize()

The only thing that differs from using any other future backend is the plan() call. The code does not have to change, it gives identical results, and it behaves exactly the same.

The mizu_multisession backend

Backend Description Alternative in future package
mizu_multisession parallel evaluation in separate R processes (on current machine) plan(multisession)

The mizu package runs parallel R workers on the local machine. Instead of communicating via sockets, the main R process and the workers exchange data via shared memory - POSIX shared memory on Linux and macOS, and Win32 file mappings on Windows.

Advantages

  • Communication between the main R process and the workers is cheap, which means that work can be split up into many small futures without the overhead dominating.

  • Large vectors and data frames are read by the workers in place, without each worker holding its own copy.

  • It works on Linux, macOS, and Windows, and requires no additional setup.

Limitations

  • The workers always run on the local machine. For workers on other machines, or on a high-performance compute (HPC) cluster, use another future backend, e.g. plan(cluster) or future.batchtools.

  • At most 64 workers are supported by mizu.

  • Data is passed via shared memory, which is limited in size. For instance, Docker containers default to only 64 MB of shared memory, which might not be enough when passing large objects.

  • Cancelling a future is advisory. A future that is already running on a worker cannot be interrupted; it runs to completion and its result is discarded.

  • Using a single worker, plan(future.mizu::mizu_multisession, workers = 1), falls back to sequential processing in the current R process, unless the number of workers is protected by I(), e.g. workers = I(1).

Installation

The package is not yet available on CRAN. To install the development version, use:

install.packages("future.mizu", repos = c("https://futureverse-devel.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
